    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.Isometry.Basic, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Isometric endomorphisms of a bilinear form #

    This file defines the predicate that an endomorphism preserves a bilinear form and provides its elementary API, including the bridge to Mathlib's bundled isometric maps. It also records that scaling two forms by the same non-zero-divisor preserves whether they are isometric (LinearMap.BilinForm.equivalent_smul_iff), and gives the evaluation lemmas LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.trans_apply, LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.symm_apply_apply and LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply for Mathlib's isometric equivalences, which map the kernel of one form onto the kernel of the other (LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.map_ker). Isometric bilinear forms have isometric associated quadratic maps (LinearMap.BilinForm.Equivalent.toQuadraticMap). The isometry group and the determinant, base-change, and orthogonal-complement API are developed in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.Isometry.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.IsIsometry {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) :
    Prop

    An endomorphism f of M is an isometry of the bilinear form B when it preserves B, that is, when B (f x) (f y) = B x y for all x and y.

    Isometric endomorphisms form a monoid, not a group: for the zero form on ℤ ^ 2 every endomorphism is one. For a finite free ℤ-module V and a left-separating integral form Q an isometric endomorphism is automatically invertible (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.IsIsometry.toIsometryGroup), and the resulting automorphisms are the arithmetic group Aut(V, Q); see LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.isometryGroup.

        theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.equivalent_smul_iff {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {M' : Type u_3} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] {C : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} {C' : LinearMap.BilinForm R M'} {a : R} (ha : a ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) :
        (a • C).Equivalent (a • C') ↔ C.Equivalent C'

        Scaling two bilinear forms by the same non-zero-divisor a neither creates nor destroys an isometry between them. In particular the constituents a • C and a • C' of two Jordan splittings are isometric exactly when their unimodular rescalings C and C' are.
